note.text: A narrative tells linked events from a chosen viewpoint. Establish the situation, introduce a change or difficulty, develop actions and provide an ending that relates to them. Time signals, pronoun reference and verb choices help the reader follow the sequence. Description should support the events, not interrupt them with an unrelated catalogue. A narrative may be invented; pupils need not disclose private incidents. A dramatic story still needs consistency in what characters know and do.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to write a coherent original narrative with setting, linked events and a meaningful ending. Builds on: paragraph planning, sentence structure and simple-past events. Leads to: past-perfect chronology and later report/narrative contrasts.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: Original model: Bih reached the fictional club room and found the notice missing. Members were gathering outside, unsure whether the meeting would happen. She checked with the teacher instead of announcing a cancellation. The room was ready; the notice had fallen behind a shelf. Bih replaced it and helped members enter. The small misunderstanding showed her why checking a source mattered more than spreading a quick guess.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Plan the setting, difficulty, actions and outcome. Choose a viewpoint and preserve it. Make transitions clear and reread each pronoun. Invent suitable details if you prefer, but do not change an object’s location or a character’s knowledge accidentally just to force the ending.

paper_task.prompt: Write an original narrative about a misunderstanding that is resolved by checking information. Use an imaginary character and setting, linked actions and a coherent ending.
model: Original model: Bih reached the fictional club room and found the notice missing. Members were gathering outside, unsure whether the meeting would happen. She checked with the teacher instead of announcing a cancellation. The room was ready; the notice had fallen behind a shelf. Bih replaced it and helped members enter. The small misunderstanding showed her why checking a source mattered more than spreading a quick guess.
checklist: My reader can follow the setting and sequence.
My viewpoint, pronouns and tenses remain coherent.
My ending grows from the problem and actions.
